transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I came in because it’s gotten kind of noticeable, I guess. Like people can see something’s off with how I’m moving. Sometimes I’m moving so slow it feels like I’m underwater—like I take forever to answer someone or even just get out of a chair.

And then other times I’m the opposite, like I’m pacing around my apartment and rubbing my hands together, like I’m trying to shake off a really bad call from work. I do customer service, so bad calls happen, but… this feels different. Sorry, I’m kind of circling around it. It’s mostly that people can actually see it now.
Have you experienced periods where you felt extremely sad or depressed?

Yeah… yeah, I have. It’s not like just a bad week or something. It’s been kind of hanging around for… a little over two years now, I think—like two years and maybe a month.

There are little stretches where it lifts a bit, like I can get through work and maybe do laundry without it feeling like this huge thing, but it doesn’t really stay gone. It eases up briefly, then comes back.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and had a lot of energy?

I don’t know… I mean, I’ve had days where I’m in a better mood, like if a customer actually says thank you or my supervisor isn’t on my case, but I wouldn’t call it extremely happy or anything. 

I do get irritated sometimes, but… I think that’s kind of normal? Like with work calls, people yelling over stuff I can’t control. But a whole period of being really energized and up like that—no, I don’t think so. At least nothing that stands out to me.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely irritable and had a lot of energy at the same time?

I’m not really sure… I mean, irritable, yes, but usually it’s tied to something, like work or someone pushing my buttons. The energy part is harder—I don’t think I’ve had that “wired and angry” thing for a whole stretch of time.

Sometimes after a bad call I’ll be kind of keyed up, but then I just sort of crash or sit there thinking about it too long. So… no, I don’t think so. Not in the way you mean, I guess.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or extremely irritable and had a lot of energy that lasted for several days or longer?

I don’t think so… not for several days. I mean, I’ve had times where I’m annoyed or I get a little more talkative if something good happens, like if a call goes smoothly or I get out of work early, but that’s not really days of, like, big energy.

Honestly I’m usually just trying to get through the day. My sleep gets weird sometimes depending on my schedule—well, and my upstairs neighbor stomps around, so that doesn’t help—but no, I can’t really point to a stretch where I was extremely happy or extremely irritable and full of energy for days.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy and had a lot of energy?

Extremely happy with a lot of energy… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had good moods, sure, like if the day goes better than expected, or if I actually get through my errands without something weird happening—like last week the grocery store was out of the coffee I like and that kind of threw me off, but that’s not what you’re asking.

So, yeah… I wouldn’t say I’ve had a period like that. Nothing where I felt unusually happy and energized in some big way.
Do you think your mood changes are related to your menstrual cycle?

Um… I’m male, so I don’t have a menstrual cycle. Unless you mean like some kind of monthly pattern in general? I haven’t really tracked it that way.

I do notice stuff lines up more with work stress or sleep being off, or just random things during the week… like if the schedule changes, that can mess with me. But menstrual cycle, no, that doesn’t really apply to me.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely irritable and had reckless or impulsive behavior?

I mean… I get irritable sometimes, yeah, like with customers repeating the same complaint or when the phone system freezes right in the middle of a call, and then I’m just sitting there listening to hold music like I don’t already hear it all day.

But reckless or impulsive? I don’t think so. Not like going out and doing dangerous stuff or making big sudden decisions. I might snap a little or want to be left alone, but I can’t think of a period where I was extremely irritable and then acting reckless because of it.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that weren't really there?

Yeah… I mean, not like seeing a person standing there or anything. But I do hear things sometimes.

It’s usually work-type stuff, which is weird because I’m not even working at that moment. Like I’ll hear the old headset beep, or a supervisor kind of voice saying my name, or something like “too slow,” and then I look over and my laptop’s closed and there’s no phone ringing. It’s… not loud like someone yelling right next to me, but it feels real enough that I check.

And then I get annoyed at myself because I’ll be like, okay, why am I still hearing that when I’m off the clock? The headset we used to have made this specific beep, too, and I hated it. Sorry, that’s probably not the point—yes, I’ve heard things that weren’t really there.
Do you ever find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or organized?

Um… I’m not totally sure what counts as “organized.” Like, if you mean can I follow a conversation, mostly yeah, I think so.

Sometimes I lose my place if I’m trying to explain something and then I start thinking about three examples at once—kind of like now, honestly. At work they want notes in a certain format, and I’ll get stuck deciding what part goes first, but that might just be normal because the software is annoying and there are all these little boxes.

So… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say my thoughts feel completely scrambled, but I do get a little scattered sometimes.
Have you ever seen things that weren't really there?

Seen things? No, not really. I don’t think I’ve seen anything that wasn’t there.

It’s more like hearing stuff, like that old headset beep from work, or a supervisor-type voice saying my name or “too slow,” and then I check and my laptop’s closed, there’s no phone ringing. But visually, no… I can’t think of anything like that.
Have you ever found that you can get by with much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

I don’t think so… I mean, my sleep is kind of all over the place sometimes, but feeling rested on less sleep? Not really something I’ve noticed.

Like, if I only sleep a few hours, I usually just feel tired and kind of useless the next day. I wish I could get by on less sleep, honestly—my neighbor upstairs seems to vacuum at the worst times, which is… not really what you asked. But no, I don’t think I get that “I barely slept and I’m totally fine” thing.
Are your symptoms interfering with your daily activities or relationships?

Yeah… I mean, I’m not completely falling apart or anything. I can still pay rent, keep food around, you know, keep a roof over my head. But it does mess with things.

Work is the main one. I’ve kind of lost momentum with steady jobs because I miss deadlines, or I avoid calls when I’m supposed to be on them, and then people start treating me like I’m unreliable. Which… I guess I am, in those moments. It’s frustrating because customer service is already one of those jobs where one missed thing turns into three, and then you’re thinking about the whole queue and the little timer and—sorry, that’s not exactly the point.

Relationships too, I guess. I see friends less. I don’t really make plans unless someone pushes me. And basic stuff slides, like meals, errands, even hiking, which I used to actually like. I can do it if I force myself, but it takes a lot more pushing than it should.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. It’s not like I decided to stop liking things, it’s more like they just don’t… catch.

I used to sketch a lot, and I’d keep these little coffee notes, like which beans tasted kind of chocolatey or burnt or whatever. And weekend hikes used to make me feel like myself. Lately I’ll open the notebook, or I’ll put my boots by the door, and I just kind of sit there. There’s nothing pulling me toward it.

Which is annoying, because the boots are right there, and I even bought new socks for hiking once—too expensive, honestly—but then I don’t go. It’s like the idea of it is still familiar, but the feeling isn’t really there.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely happy or irritable and your thoughts were racing?

I’m not sure… I mean, I get irritated, sure, but I don’t know if it’s that kind of “extremely” irritated thing you mean.

And happy… not really in a big way. My thoughts can feel busy sometimes, like I’ll be thinking about a bill, then a work message, then whether I forgot laundry in the washer — which I actually did once and had to rewash everything because it got that smell — but I don’t know if I’d call it racing.

So… I guess I haven’t noticed a clear period like that.
Have you ever had a period where your hallucinations, such as hearing voices, were particularly vivid or disturbing?

Yeah… sometimes it’s more noticeable than other times. Like I’ll hear the old headset beep, that little work call sound, even when my laptop’s closed and there’s no phone ringing or anything.

Or I’ll hear this supervisor-type voice say my name, or say “too slow,” which is… not great. It’s weird because I know the actual supervisor isn’t there, and half the time I’m not even working. It still kind of makes my stomach drop, like I’m behind on a queue again. Customer service timers are honestly awful—sorry, I know that’s not the point.

So, yeah, it can be disturbing, mostly because it feels so specific. Like it’s using work stuff against me.
Have you ever felt like you're worthless or have a low opinion of yourself?

Yeah… I do. Probably more than I want to admit.

It’s usually over small stuff, like at work if I reply too slowly or I miss some little detail, I’ll keep replaying it after. Or with contract jobs I’ve done, I’ll think, okay, that one message took too long, so I must’ve let everyone down. And then my brain goes from that to, like, well, maybe I deserved to lose the job or get fired.

Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, because sometimes it’s just one email or one customer ticket, but it doesn’t feel small in my head. It turns into this whole… proof that I’m not really good enough.
Have you ever felt extremely happy or extremely irritable for several days in a row?

I don’t think so… not for several days in a row.

I mean, I can get irritable, like if something keeps beeping or there’s some customer email that’s worded in that passive-aggressive way—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But it doesn’t feel like this big several-day stretch where I’m just extremely happy or angry the whole time.

Extremely happy, definitely not that I can remember. More like normal little moments, if anything. So… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you ever felt extremely irritable for several days in a row?

Not really, no. I mean, I get annoyed in the moment—like if there’s a weird work message or I’m already tired and something stupid happens with the system—but it usually doesn’t last days.

I might complain about it too much, honestly. Like I’ll tell myself I’m just being “efficient” by noticing all the broken processes, but sometimes I’m just irritated. But several days in a row where I’m extremely irritable? I don’t think so. Nothing that stands out like that.
Have you ever had a period where your hallucinations were so real that you acted on them as if they were real?

Kind of… I mean, I’ve definitely reacted to it at first like it was real.

Like I’ll hear the old headset beep, the one from work, or a supervisor-type voice saying my name or “too slow,” even when my laptop is closed and there’s no phone ringing. And I’ll sort of look around or check the laptop like, wait, did I miss something?

It’s weird because my brain goes into work mode immediately. Customer service stuff does that anyway—those little alert sounds get burned into your head. But then I realize, no, nothing’s actually on, so… I don’t know if that counts as “acting on it,” but I have responded to it like it was happening for a moment.

Not really, no. I mean, I get annoyed in the moment—like if there’s a weird work message or I’m already tired and something stupid happens with the system—but it usually doesn’t last days.

I might complain about it too much, honestly. Like I’ll tell myself I’m just being “efficient” by noticing all the broken processes, but sometimes I’m just irritated. But several days in a row where I’m extremely irritable? I don’t think so. Nothing that stands out like that.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for a psychotic episode
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period where your hallucinations were so real that you acted on them as if they were real?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I’ll hear the old headset beep or a supervisor-type voice say my name or 'too slow' when my laptop is closed and there’s no phone ringing.
target_item.reason: The question directly asks about hallucinations feeling real and whether they influenced behavior.

patient.answer:
Kind of… I mean, I’ve definitely reacted to it at first like it was real.

Like I’ll hear the old headset beep, the one from work, or a supervisor-type voice saying my name or “too slow,” even when my laptop is closed and there’s no phone ringing. And I’ll sort of look around or check the laptop like, wait, did I miss something?

It’s weird because my brain goes into work mode immediately. Customer service stuff does that anyway—those little alert sounds get burned into your head. But then I realize, no, nothing’s actually on, so… I don’t know if that counts as “acting on it,” but I have responded to it like it was happening for a moment.
